title: spec: migration entry cbp-optional-master-admitted still says writes leaving the optional master empty are refused with 422 (the write gate admits them since #31082)
body:
domain:devx#2 · marchtian · session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8

Filing gate: ① a defect, measured by reading the code. Found while writing the docs for #31095 (dev report 6709055161, PR #31164). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade and the lane.
Reader: the `domain:spec` lane, file `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cbp-optional-master-admitted.ts`. Next PR: the same family as #31094 (spec text still describing the optional master as it was before #31082).
Dedupe (open AND closed): "cbp-optional-master-admitted" → 1 hit, #31095. That card is the docs pages, not this entry. #30977 (closed) is a different conversion. #31094 is `security-service.ts` jsdoc, not this entry.
class: b (release-text) · reach: every reader of the spec migration registry (`os migrate meta`, the release notes generated from entries).

## What is wrong

At `main` `56baf78e0c`, the entry's `replacement` (lines 24–25) says:

> Writes are unchanged by this entry: an insert or update that leaves the master reference empty is still refused with 422.

Since `037371559b` (#31082, card #30906), the write gate admits those writes. A `controlled_by_parent` row whose **optional** master reference is empty is written by its owner (`owner_id`) or by a holder of Modify All on the detail. Everyone else gets `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, not 422. Only a **required** master's empty reference is still `422 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`. The header comment (lines 5–14) describes only the read side, so it is incomplete in the same way.

## Wanted

- Reword the `replacement` (and the header comment) to the current rule:
  - a required master's empty reference is still refused with 422;
  - an optional master's empty reference is written by the owner or Modify All on the detail, and refused with 403 for everyone else.
- Cite #31082 where the entry cites the read side.
- Take the wording that #31092's permissions pages and PR #31164's docs pages use, so the four texts agree.
- Keep the entry's `id` and `surface`. Whether this needs an entry-text changeset is the spec lane's house rule.
